newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq raps planned Turkey exercise with Israel, U.S.
newsitem.headline: Iraq raps planned Turkey exercise with Israel, U.S.

text.p: Iraqi Foreign Minister Mohammad Saeed al-Sahaf, in remarks published on Friday, sharply criticised Turkey for proposed naval exercises with Israel and the United States.
"Iraq strongly denounces these manoeuvres and considers them a provocative and hostile act against the Arab nation," Sahaf said in a statement carried by Iraqi newspapers on Friday.
"The participation of a state (Turkey) whose people are Moslems with the Zionist entity...is not an ordinary act," Sahaf said.
He urged Arab countries to confront "such mistaken policies before they are enlarged" and called on Turkey to "reconsider its participation in these military exercises."

A series of recent high-level talks between Israel and Turkish defence planners and top brass has accelerated the pace of growing security ties between the two regional powers, despite the opposition of Turkey's Islamist prime minister.
In talks earlier this week Turkish Deputy Chief of Staff General Cevik Bir met Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai to discuss joint naval exercises with Israel and the United States.
This in turn has touch off alarm in Middle East capitals, fearful of an emerging axis between Ankara and the Jewish state, backed up by U.S. military muscle.

Israel and Turkey have taken pains to say their ties are not aimed at any third country, and a Turkish spokesman said on Wednesday the proposed naval exercises would involve search and rescue operations only.
